name: dates
description: Calendar helpers on Time and Zone: boundaries, business days, ISO weeks, ranges, intervals, periods, RFC 2822, HTTP-date and ISO durations

api.name: Period
api.sig: pub type Period = {years: Int, months: Int, weeks: Int, days: Int, hours: Int, minutes: Int, seconds: Int, millis: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A calendar period: the parts of an ISO 8601 duration. Years and months have no fixed length,
so they are applied with Time.add_months (clamping the day to the month's end); weeks and days
are 7 and 1 days of 24 hours; the rest are exact. Parts may be negative.

api.name: Interval
api.sig: pub type Interval = {start: Time, end: Time} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A half-open span of time, from `start` (included) to `end` (excluded), with `start <= end`.

api.name: IsoWeek
api.sig: pub type IsoWeek = {year: Int, week: Int, weekday: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
An ISO 8601 week date: the ISO week-numbering `year`, the `week` (1 to 53) and the `weekday`
(1 is Monday).

api.name: CalUnit
api.sig: pub type CalUnit = Days | Weeks | Months | Quarters | Years derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The unit of a step in a date range, or of add_units.

api.name: BusinessCalendar
api.sig: pub type BusinessCalendar = {weekend: List[Int], holidays: List[Time]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Which days are business days: the weekdays of the weekend (1 is Monday, 7 Sunday) and a list
of holidays (only their UTC dates count).

api.name: is_leap_year
api.sig: fn is_leap_year(y: Int) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `y` is a leap year in the proleptic Gregorian calendar (year 0 is a leap year).

api.name: days_in_month
api.sig: fn days_in_month(y: Int, m: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 12) -> Int
api.doc: The number of days in month `m` (1 to 12) of year `y`.

api.name: days_in_year
api.sig: fn days_in_year(y: Int) -> Int
api.doc: The number of days in year `y`: 365 or 366.

api.name: quarter
api.sig: fn quarter(t: Time) -> Int
api.doc: The quarter of the year `t` is in (UTC): 1 for January to March, up to 4.

api.name: weekday_name
api.sig: fn weekday_name(d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Str
api.doc: The English name of weekday `d` (1 is Monday): "Monday" to "Sunday".

api.name: weekday_abbr
api.sig: fn weekday_abbr(d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Str
api.doc: The three-letter English abbreviation of weekday `d`: "Mon" to "Sun".

api.name: month_name
api.sig: fn month_name(m: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 12) -> Str
api.doc: The English name of month `m`: "January" to "December".

api.name: month_abbr
api.sig: fn month_abbr(m: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 12) -> Str
api.doc: The three-letter English abbreviation of month `m`: "Jan" to "Dec".

api.name: epoch_day
api.sig: fn epoch_day(t: Time) -> Int
api.doc: The number of days from 1970-01-01 to the UTC date of `t`, rounded down (negative before 1970).

api.name: from_epoch_day
api.sig: fn from_epoch_day(n: Int) -> Time
api.doc: Midnight UTC of the date `n` days after 1970-01-01.

api.name: same_day
api.sig: fn same_day(a: Time, b: Time) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `a` and `b` fall on the same UTC date.

api.name: same_day_in
api.sig: fn same_day_in(a: Time, b: Time, z: Zone) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `a` and `b` fall on the same local date in zone `z`.

api.name: is_weekend
api.sig: fn is_weekend(t: Time) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `t` is on a Saturday or a Sunday (UTC).

api.name: start_of_day
api.sig: fn start_of_day(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: Midnight UTC at the start of `t`'s date.

api.name: end_of_day
api.sig: fn end_of_day(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of `t`'s UTC date (23:59:59.999).

api.name: start_of_week
api.sig: fn start_of_week(t: Time, first: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc:
Midnight at the start of the week containing `t`, where weeks start on weekday `first`
(1 is Monday, as in ISO 8601; 7 is Sunday, as in the US).

api.name: end_of_week
api.sig: fn end_of_week(t: Time, first: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of the week containing `t`, where weeks start on weekday `first`.

api.name: start_of_month
api.sig: fn start_of_month(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: Midnight UTC on the first day of `t`'s month.

api.name: end_of_month
api.sig: fn end_of_month(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of `t`'s month (UTC).

api.name: start_of_quarter
api.sig: fn start_of_quarter(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: Midnight UTC on the first day of `t`'s quarter (January, April, July or October 1).

api.name: end_of_quarter
api.sig: fn end_of_quarter(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of `t`'s quarter (UTC).

api.name: start_of_year
api.sig: fn start_of_year(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: Midnight UTC on January 1 of `t`'s year.

api.name: end_of_year
api.sig: fn end_of_year(t: Time) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of `t`'s year (UTC): December 31, 23:59:59.999.

api.name: resolve_local
api.sig: fn resolve_local(z: Zone, wall: Time) -> Time
api.doc:
The instant at which the wall clock of zone `z` shows `wall` (a Time whose UTC fields are read
as local fields, as Zone.local returns). In an overlap (clocks turned back) it is the earlier
instant; in a gap (clocks turned forward, so `wall` never shows) it is the first instant after
the gap, the moment the clocks jump.

api.name: start_of_day_in
api.sig: fn start_of_day_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc:
The first instant of `t`'s local date in zone `z` (usually local midnight; where midnight
falls in a DST gap, the first instant after the gap).

api.name: end_of_day_in
api.sig: fn end_of_day_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc:
The last millisecond of `t`'s local date in zone `z`: one millisecond before the start of the
next local date, so a day can be 23 or 25 hours long.

api.name: start_of_week_in
api.sig: fn start_of_week_in(t: Time, z: Zone, first: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: The first instant of the local week containing `t` in zone `z`, weeks starting on `first`.

api.name: end_of_week_in
api.sig: fn end_of_week_in(t: Time, z: Zone, first: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of the local week containing `t` in zone `z`, weeks starting on `first`.

api.name: start_of_month_in
api.sig: fn start_of_month_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc: The first instant of `t`'s local month in zone `z`.

api.name: end_of_month_in
api.sig: fn end_of_month_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of `t`'s local month in zone `z`.

api.name: start_of_quarter_in
api.sig: fn start_of_quarter_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc: The first instant of `t`'s local quarter in zone `z`.

api.name: end_of_quarter_in
api.sig: fn end_of_quarter_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of `t`'s local quarter in zone `z`.

api.name: start_of_year_in
api.sig: fn start_of_year_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc: The first instant of `t`'s local year in zone `z`.

api.name: end_of_year_in
api.sig: fn end_of_year_in(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc: The last millisecond of `t`'s local year in zone `z`.

api.name: local_date
api.sig: fn local_date(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Time
api.doc:
The local date of `t` in zone `z`, as midnight UTC of that date (for date arithmetic and
comparisons that should ignore the zone afterwards).

api.name: standard_calendar
api.sig: fn standard_calendar(holidays: List[Time]) -> BusinessCalendar
api.doc: A calendar with Saturday and Sunday as the weekend and the given holidays.

api.name: is_business_day
api.sig: fn is_business_day(t: Time, cal: BusinessCalendar) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether the UTC date of `t` is a business day of `cal`: not a weekend day and not a holiday.

api.name: add_business_days
api.sig: fn add_business_days(t: Time, n: Int, cal: BusinessCalendar) -> Time
api.doc:
`t` moved by `n` business days of `cal` (backwards when `n` is negative), keeping the time of
day. Counting starts from the day after (or before) `t`, so `t` itself need not be a business
day; `n == 0` returns `t` unchanged. The weekend must leave at least one business day a week.

api.name: business_days_between
api.sig: fn business_days_between(a: Time, b: Time, cal: BusinessCalendar) -> Int
api.doc:
The number of business days of `cal` from the date of `a` (included) to the date of `b`
(excluded); negative when `b` is before `a`. Times of day are ignored.

api.name: next_business_day
api.sig: fn next_business_day(t: Time, cal: BusinessCalendar) -> Time
api.doc: The first business day of `cal` strictly after `t`'s date, keeping the time of day.

api.name: previous_business_day
api.sig: fn previous_business_day(t: Time, cal: BusinessCalendar) -> Time
api.doc: The last business day of `cal` strictly before `t`'s date, keeping the time of day.

api.name: roll_forward
api.sig: fn roll_forward(t: Time, cal: BusinessCalendar) -> Time
api.doc: `t` if it is a business day of `cal`, else the next business day (the "following" convention).

api.name: roll_backward
api.sig: fn roll_backward(t: Time, cal: BusinessCalendar) -> Time
api.doc: `t` if it is a business day of `cal`, else the previous business day ("preceding").

api.name: next_weekday
api.sig: fn next_weekday(t: Time, d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: The first instant after `t` that is on weekday `d`, at the same time of day: 1 to 7 days later.

api.name: previous_weekday
api.sig: fn previous_weekday(t: Time, d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: The last instant before `t` that is on weekday `d`, at the same time of day: 1 to 7 days earlier.

api.name: next_or_same_weekday
api.sig: fn next_or_same_weekday(t: Time, d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: `t` if it is on weekday `d`, else next_weekday(t, d).

api.name: previous_or_same_weekday
api.sig: fn previous_or_same_weekday(t: Time, d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: `t` if it is on weekday `d`, else previous_weekday(t, d).

api.name: nth_weekday
api.sig: fn nth_weekday(y: Int, m: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 12, d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7, n: Int where _ != 0 and _ >= -5 and _ <= 5) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
The `n`th weekday `d` of month `m` of year `y`, at midnight UTC: `n` is 1 to 5 counting from
the start (3 and Monday is the third Monday), or -1 to -5 counting from the end (-1 and Friday
is the last Friday). `none` when the month has no such day (a fifth Monday).

api.name: last_weekday
api.sig: fn last_weekday(y: Int, m: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 12, d: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 7) -> Time
api.doc: The last weekday `d` of month `m` of year `y`, at midnight UTC (the last Friday).

api.name: easter
api.sig: fn easter(y: Int where _ >= 1) -> Time
api.doc:
Western (Gregorian) Easter Sunday of year `y`, at midnight UTC, by the anonymous Gregorian
algorithm (Meeus, Jones, Butcher). It is computed for any year from 1, proleptically before 1583.

api.name: iso_week
api.sig: fn iso_week(t: Time) -> IsoWeek
api.doc:
The ISO 8601 week date of `t` (UTC): weeks start on Monday and week 1 is the week with the
year's first Thursday, so early January can be in the previous year's week 52 or 53 and late
December in the next year's week 1.

api.name: iso_weeks_in_year
api.sig: fn iso_weeks_in_year(y: Int) -> Int
api.doc:
The number of ISO weeks in ISO year `y`: 53 when January 1 is a Thursday, or a Wednesday in a
leap year, else 52.

api.name: from_iso_week
api.sig: fn from_iso_week(y: Int, w: Int, d: Int) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc: Midnight UTC of ISO week date (`y`, `w`, `d`); `none` when the week or weekday is out of range.

api.name: format_iso_week
api.sig: fn format_iso_week(t: Time) -> Str
api.doc: The ISO week date of `t` as text: "2026-W42-5".

api.name: parse_iso_week
api.sig: fn parse_iso_week(s: Str) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
Parses an ISO week date, extended ("2026-W42-5", "2026-W42") or basic ("2026W425", "2026W42");
a missing weekday is Monday. `none` for anything else or a week the year doesn't have.

api.name: format_ordinal_date
api.sig: fn format_ordinal_date(t: Time) -> Str
api.doc: The ordinal date of `t` (UTC) as text: year and day of the year, "2026-289".

api.name: from_ordinal
api.sig: fn from_ordinal(y: Int, n: Int) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc: Midnight UTC of day `n` (1 to 365 or 366) of year `y`; `none` when `n` is out of range.

api.name: parse_ordinal_date
api.sig: fn parse_ordinal_date(s: Str) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc: Parses an ordinal date, "2026-289" or "2026289".

api.name: add_units
api.sig: fn add_units(t: Time, n: Int, unit: CalUnit) -> Time
api.doc:
`t` moved by `n` units (backwards when negative). Months, quarters and years use
Time.add_months, which clamps the day to the end of the month (January 31 plus one month is
February 28 or 29); days and weeks are exact multiples of 24 hours.

api.name: date_range
api.sig: fn date_range(start: Time, end: Time, every: Int where _ > 0, unit: CalUnit) -> List[Time]
api.doc:
The times `start`, `start + every units`, `start + 2 * every units`, ... that are before `end`
(`end` excluded); empty when `end <= start`. Each element is computed from `start`
(add_units(start, k * every, unit)), so a monthly range from January 31 gives February 28,
March 31, April 30 rather than drifting to the 28th.

api.name: date_range_inclusive
api.sig: fn date_range_inclusive(start: Time, end: Time, every: Int where _ > 0, unit: CalUnit) -> List[Time]
api.doc: Like date_range but `end` is included when the steps land on it exactly.

api.name: days_between
api.sig: fn days_between(a: Time, b: Time) -> Int
api.doc:
The number of calendar days from the UTC date of `a` to the UTC date of `b` (negative when `b`
is earlier); times of day are ignored.

api.name: months_between
api.sig: fn months_between(a: Time, b: Time) -> Int
api.doc:
The number of whole months from `a` to `b`: the largest `m` with a.add_months(m) <= b, or the
negation of months_between(b, a) when `b` is before `a`.

api.name: years_between
api.sig: fn years_between(a: Time, b: Time) -> Int
api.doc: The number of whole years from `a` to `b`, by the rule of months_between.

api.name: age
api.sig: fn age(birth: Time, on: Time) -> Int
api.doc:
The age in whole years on date `on` of someone born on `birth`, from their dates (UTC; times
of day are ignored). A February 29 birthday is reached on February 28 in common years.
Negative when `on` is before `birth`.

api.name: diff
api.sig: fn diff(a: Time, b: Time) -> Period
api.doc:
The calendar difference from `a` to `b` as years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds and
milliseconds (weeks 0), such that add_period(a, diff(a, b)) == b when `a <= b` (except when a
month end clamps). When `b` is before `a` every part is negated from diff(b, a).

api.name: interval
api.sig: fn interval(a: Time, b: Time) -> Opt[Interval]
api.doc: The interval from `a` to `b`; `none` when `b` is before `a`.

api.name: interval_length
api.sig: fn interval_length(iv: Interval) -> Duration
api.doc: The length of interval `iv`.

api.name: interval_is_empty
api.sig: fn interval_is_empty(iv: Interval) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `iv` is empty (its start equals its end).

api.name: covers
api.sig: fn covers(iv: Interval, t: Time) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether instant `t` is in `iv`: start <= t < end.

api.name: encloses
api.sig: fn encloses(outer: Interval, inner: Interval) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `outer` contains all of `inner`.

api.name: overlaps
api.sig: fn overlaps(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `a` and `b` share some instant (empty intervals overlap nothing).

api.name: abuts
api.sig: fn abuts(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether one interval ends exactly where the other starts.

api.name: intersection
api.sig: fn intersection(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Opt[Interval]
api.doc: The part `a` and `b` share; `none` when they don't overlap.

api.name: gap
api.sig: fn gap(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Opt[Interval]
api.doc: The interval between `a` and `b` when they are apart; `none` when they overlap or abut.

api.name: hull
api.sig: fn hull(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval
api.doc: The smallest interval that contains both `a` and `b`.

api.name: merge_intervals
api.sig: fn merge_intervals(xs: List[Interval]) -> List[Interval]
api.doc: The intervals sorted by start, with overlapping and abutting ones merged; empty ones dropped.

api.name: period_zero
api.sig: fn period_zero() -> Period
api.doc: The period with every part 0.

api.name: negate_period
api.sig: fn negate_period(p: Period) -> Period
api.doc: The period with every part of `p` negated.

api.name: period_is_zero
api.sig: fn period_is_zero(p: Period) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every part of `p` is 0.

api.name: add_period
api.sig: fn add_period(t: Time, p: Period) -> Time
api.doc:
`t` moved by period `p`: first the years and months together with Time.add_months (clamping
the day to the month's end), then the weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds as
exact durations.

api.name: period_duration
api.sig: fn period_duration(p: Period) -> Opt[Duration]
api.doc: The exact length of `p` when it has no years or months (days count 24 hours); `none` otherwise.

api.name: duration_period
api.sig: fn duration_period(d: Duration) -> Period
api.doc:
Duration `d` split into days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds (no weeks, months or
years); every part has the sign of `d`.

api.name: format_iso_duration
api.sig: fn format_iso_duration(p: Period) -> Str
api.doc:
`p` as an ISO 8601 duration: "P1Y2M3DT4H5M6.5S", "P2W", "PT0S" for zero. When every non-zero part
is negative the text starts with "-" ("-P1D"); mixed signs are written per part ("P1M-2D"), as
java.time does. Milliseconds are written as a fraction of the seconds.

api.name: parse_iso_duration
api.sig: fn parse_iso_duration(s: Str) -> Opt[Period]
api.doc:
Parses an ISO 8601 duration: "P1Y2M10DT2H30M", "PT1.5S", "P3W", "-P1D", "P1M-2D". Units must
come in the order Y M W D, then "T" and H M S; at least one part is required, and "T" must be
followed by one. Only seconds may have a fraction ("." or ","), kept to milliseconds and
truncated beyond. A leading "-" negates every part. `none` for anything else, or for a value
that does not fit an Int.

api.name: unix_seconds
api.sig: fn unix_seconds(t: Time) -> Int
api.doc: The Unix time of `t` in whole seconds, rounded down.

api.name: from_unix_seconds
api.sig: fn from_unix_seconds(s: Int) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc: The time `s` seconds after 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z; `none` when `s * 1000` overflows an Int.

api.name: format_rfc3339
api.sig: fn format_rfc3339(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Str
api.doc:
`t` as RFC 3339 text in zone `z`, with milliseconds only when they are not 0:
"2026-10-16T21:43:27+05:30", "2026-10-16T16:13:27.123Z" in UTC.

api.name: parse_rfc3339
api.sig: fn parse_rfc3339(s: Str) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
Parses an RFC 3339 timestamp: date, "T" (or "t" or a space), hours, minutes and seconds, an
optional fraction (kept to milliseconds, truncated beyond), and "Z" or an offset "+05:30". A
leap second (":60") is rejected, as Time can't hold one. Stricter than the builtin parse_time,
which also takes dates alone and offsets without minutes.

api.name: format_rfc2822
api.sig: fn format_rfc2822(t: Time, z: Zone) -> Str
api.doc: `t` as an RFC 5322 (RFC 2822) date in zone `z`: "Fri, 16 Oct 2026 21:43:27 +0530".

api.name: parse_rfc2822
api.sig: fn parse_rfc2822(s: Str) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
Parses an RFC 5322 (RFC 2822) date: an optional weekday and comma, a day of one or two
digits, an English month abbreviation, a year (four digits; the obsolete two-digit years are
2000 to 2049 for 00 to 49 and 1950 to 1999 for 50 to 99, three-digit years add 1900), hours
and minutes with optional seconds, and a zone: "+0530", "-0000", or the obsolete "UT", "GMT",
"Z", "EST", "EDT", "CST", "CDT", "MST", "MDT", "PST", "PDT" (military letters count as +0000,
as RFC 5322 says). Names are case-insensitive, comments in parentheses and extra whitespace are
ignored. A weekday that doesn't match the date gives `none`.

api.name: format_http_date
api.sig: fn format_http_date(t: Time) -> Str
api.doc:
`t` as an HTTP date (IMF-fixdate, RFC 9110 section 5.6.7), always in GMT:
"Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT".

api.name: parse_http_date
api.sig: fn parse_http_date(s: Str) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
Parses an HTTP date in the three forms RFC 9110 requires recipients to accept: IMF-fixdate
("Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT"), the obsolete RFC 850 form ("Sunday, 06-Nov-94 08:49:37
GMT", two-digit years 00 to 69 are 2000 to 2069 and 70 to 99 are 1970 to 1999) and asctime
("Sun Nov  6 08:49:37 1994"). Names are case-sensitive, as the RFC specifies. A weekday that
doesn't match the date gives `none`.

api.name: parse_format
api.sig: fn parse_format(s: Str, pat: Str) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
Parses `s` by strftime pattern `pat`, the directives Time.format writes plus %z: %Y (four
digits), %m %d %H %M %S (two digits), %L (three-digit milliseconds), %j (three-digit day of the
year), %u (weekday digit, 1 is Monday), %a %A %b %B (English names, case-insensitive), %F
(%Y-%m-%d), %T (%H:%M:%S), %z ("Z", "+0530" or "+05:30") and %%; every other character must
match itself. Missing fields default to 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000 UTC; %j sets the month and day
unless %m or %d is given, and then they must agree. A weekday that disagrees with the date,
an unknown directive, an invalid date or leftover text gives `none`. Zone names (%Z) can't be
parsed, since abbreviations are ambiguous.

api.name: relative_date
api.sig: fn relative_date(t: Time, now: Time, z: Zone) -> Str
api.doc:
How the local date of `t` relates to the local date of `now` in zone `z`, in words: "today",
"yesterday", "tomorrow", a weekday within six days ("last Tuesday", "next Friday"), "last week"
or "next week" (7 to 13 days), "3 weeks ago" or "in 2 weeks" (under a month), "last month",
"in 5 months", "last year", "in 3 years". Times of day are ignored; whole months and years are
counted by months_between of the local dates.

api.name: relative_days
api.sig: fn relative_days(t: Time, now: Time, z: Zone) -> Str
api.doc:
Like relative_date but with numbers instead of weekday names and "last"/"next": "today",
"yesterday", "tomorrow", "3 days ago", "in 5 days", "1 week ago", "in 2 months", "4 years ago".
